reasons: Deviation is correctly identified: the term is open-ended (§2 runs until terminated under §6), yet the only convenience right in p0032 is conditioned on there being no uncompleted Statement of Work, so Company has no ability to exit an in-flight engagement — the missing-behaviour deviation the rule contemplates — and there is no prepaid-fee refund.

The Contractor-side call is also supportable: a 15-day convenience right sits below the rule's 90-day floor, and the redline moves it to 90 days' notice and keeps it limited to periods between Statements of Work, matching the fallback/preferred stance that Vendor cannot walk mid-term.

The redline reaches the preferred position with a coherent single-clause rewrite: Company may terminate the Agreement or any SOW, in whole or in part, on 30 days' written notice with refund of prepaid fees and no early-termination penalty.

Failed check 'Customer convenience termination present' is a phrasing artefact — the added sentence uses the contract's existing 'for any or no reason' formulation rather than the words 'for convenience', and 'Company' is a Customer alias; substance is present.

Changed-character ratio of 0.756 is justified here because the rule requires both inserting a new Customer right and re-scoping the existing mutual 15-day right; the surrounding SOW-conditioned language is preserved for Contractor only.
Comment is accurate, correctly explains the two changes and the open-ended-term rationale, and offers the 60-day fallback; tone and prefix conform.

Minor, non-blocking: the rewrite also drops Company's existing 15-day exit when no SOW is outstanding (replacing it with the 30-day right) and adds a 'no further liability' sentence beyond the model language — both are net-favourable to us but could be trimmed if a strictly minimal edit is preferred.
